report.summary: Chunk 2 of graph_delta.py: helper functions, measure(), run(), render(), main(), and start of held_out(); all docstring claims verified against this chunk.
risks: main() --held-out branch | medium | held_out() is defined below main() but the module-level import in the branch resolves it; however, the comment claims the specificity arm was unreachable due to late binding, and the --held-out branch has the same late-binding pattern but is not flagged as unreachable. | Check if held_out is defined before main() in the file (outside this chunk).

measure() | medium | If _ast_refs returns an error, skipped_reason is set but layers continue to be appended and applied stays True; this may report a skipped-but-applied result. | Inspect _ast_refs error semantics and how run() counts applied vs skipped.

render() | low | The header line uses rep['detected']/rep['applied'] but the LEAKY arm line uses rep['detected_leaky']/rep['applied']; if detected_leaky is not a subset of detected, the gap line may be misleading. | Verify that detected_leaky is always a subset of detected.

main() --specificity branch | medium | The comment says specificity, commit_shas, and measure_commit were defined below the if __name__ block, but this chunk shows main() with a late-binding import for specificity. The comment may be stale or the fix may be incomplete. | Check if commit_shas and measure_commit are still defined below the if __name__ block.

held_out() | medium | The docstring claims the corpus is built from the tree by rule with no knowledge of scoring layers, but this chunk only shows the docstring and the import of generate; the actual generation logic is in another module. | Inspect daedalus/eval/mutate.py generate() to verify independence.

handoff.purpose: Implements per-mutation measurement, corpus-level run/render, CLI entry, and starts the held-out evaluator.

symbols.name: _structure_by_function
symbols.note: Parses Python text, walks AST, counts node class names at depths for each function. Skips docstrings, ignores Name/Constant/Load/Store/Del nodes, caps depth at 24.

symbols.name: _structure_keys
symbols.note: Builds a set of 'fn:shape#index' keys from _structure_by_function counters.

symbols.name: _units_and_refs
symbols.note: Extracts units via parse_mod.extract_units and builds refs set of 'unit->identifier' pairs from graph_mod.identifiers.

symbols.name: _type_edge_keys
symbols.note: Builds type-layer keys from parse_mod.python_type_facts; returns empty set on AttributeError or SyntaxError.

symbols.name: measure
symbols.note: Applies a mutation in memory and computes layer deltas: leaky refs, AST refs, literals, structure, types, and data.literals (optional). Sets skipped_reason on read failure, missing anchor, or AST parse error.

symbols.name: run
symbols.note: Loads mutations, measures each, aggregates counts by defect class, returns a summary dict with skipped reasons, detected counts, missed list, and full results.

symbols.name: render
symbols.note: Formats the run() result dict into a human-readable report string.

symbols.name: main
symbols.note: CLI entry. Handles --held-out, --specificity, and default run. Writes JSON reports to runs/eval/.

symbols.name: held_out
symbols.note: Docstring-only in this chunk; the body begins with an import from .mutate. Intended to evaluate detection on a mechanically generated corpus.

claims.text: moves the reference layer and not this one, and a change that wraps a statement in ``if not ...`` moves this one and not the others.
claims.why: The docstring is truncated; the full claim about which changes move which layers cannot be evaluated from the visible fragment.
The `if depth > 24: return` guard limits recursion depth, protecting against deeply nested ASTs.

claims.text: Names and constants are the OTHER layers' business. Recording only the node class is what keeps the three signals independent.
claims.why: The code explicitly skips ast.Name, ast.Constant, ast.Load, ast.Store, ast.Del children, recording only node class names.

claims.text: Per-unit identifier references — the name-based call view, one file wide.
claims.why: The function extracts units and builds refs as 'u.name->name' pairs for identifiers in each unit.

claims.text: Whole-repo resolution is deliberately not used: the question is whether the graph MOVES, and a single file answers that far more cheaply than two index builds.
claims.why: The function only processes the given module file; no repository-wide index is built.

claims.text: A cross-file consequence would only ADD movement, so measuring one file is the conservative direction.
claims.why: This is a reasoning claim about cross-file effects; the chunk cannot observe whether cross-file resolution would add movement.

claims.text: Uses the same extraction the index uses.
claims.why: The chunk calls parse_mod.python_type_facts but cannot verify that this matches the index's extraction method.

claims.text: Degrades to an empty set for a language with no type vocabulary — which is reported, never silently treated as 'nothing changed'.
claims.why: The function returns set() on AttributeError or SyntaxError, and the caller measure() appends a LayerDelta with empty added/removed. There is no reporting of the degradation; the layer simply appears unchanged.

claims.text: Apply one mutation IN MEMORY and report what moved. Nothing is written.
claims.why: measure() reads the file, replaces text in memory, and never writes to disk. No filesystem write calls are present.

claims.text: The corpus is pinned to a revision; a drifted anchor is a real finding about the corpus, not a licence to fuzzy-match into place.
claims.where: comment in measure() near the find check
claims.why: If mutation.find is not in before, the function sets skipped_reason and returns without applying the mutation.

claims.text: LEAKY arm: raw-source identifiers, comments included. Kept on purpose -- the gap between the two arms IS the measured size of the marker artefact.
claims.why: The leaky arm uses _units_and_refs, which uses parse_mod.extract_units and graph_mod.identifiers on raw source (comments included), while the AST arm uses _ast_refs which excludes comments.

claims.text: CLEAN arm: AST identifiers. Comments are not tokens here.
claims.why: The code uses _ast_refs, which parses the AST; comments are not part of the AST.

claims.text: Skipped mutants are NOT counted as misses and NOT counted as passes. An anchor that no longer matches means the corpus drifted; folding that into either column would turn a bookkeeping problem into a result.
claims.why: run() separates 'skipped' (results where applied is False) from 'missed' (applied but not detected), and the summary counts only applied results for detected/missed.

claims.text: MEASURED 2026-07-30: `specificity`, `commit_shas` and `measure_commit` are defined BELOW the `if __name__` block and this function is defined above them, so no committed command could reach the specificity arm at all.
claims.why: The chunk shows main() with a late-binding import for specificity, but cannot see whether commit_shas and measure_commit are defined below the if __name__ block.

claims.text: The published false-alarm figures (0.9% refs, 0.7% structure) were produced by a throwaway script during a session and could not be regenerated by anyone afterwards -- a measurement without a command is a measurement without provenance, which this repository treats as no measurement.
claims.why: This is a historical claim about figures and scripts outside this chunk.

claims.text: Detection rate over a MECHANICALLY generated corpus, per operator.
claims.why: The body of held_out() is not shown; only the docstring and the import line are present.

claims.text: MEASURED 2026-07-30, and the reason this exists as a function rather than as a number in a document: the published 75.3% held-out figure had **no committed command**.
claims.why: The claim references historical measurements and the function's existence; the chunk cannot verify the provenance claim.

claims.text: Held out in the meaningful sense: :mod:`daedalus.eval.mutate` builds the corpus from the tree by rule, with no knowledge of what the scoring layers look at, so nothing here was tuned against these specific mutants.
claims.why: The generation logic is in another module (daedalus.eval.mutate), not visible in this chunk.

claims.text: Scored on the CLEAN arm only. The three layers are applied to a function's source before and after mutation, and a mutant counts as detected if any of them moves.
claims.why: The scoring logic is in the body of held_out(), which is not shown in this chunk.

observations.what: _type_edge_keys returns empty set on AttributeError/SyntaxError, but the docstring claims the degradation is 'reported'. There is no reporting mechanism; the caller measure() treats it as an empty layer, indistinguishable from 'no change'.

measure() sets skipped_reason if _ast_refs returns an error, but still appends the layer and leaves applied=True. This could lead to a result that is both applied and skipped, which is not handled by run()'s classification.

main() --held-out branch calls held_out() which is defined later in the file, but the comment only mentions late binding for specificity, commit_shas, and measure_commit. The late-binding pattern is identical for held_out, yet the comment does not flag it as unreachable.

The render() function excludes 'code.refs.leaky' from the moved layers, but the header line still shows detected_leaky/applied. This may present the leaky arm as a separate metric while hiding which layers moved for it.
